notes: Technical board. Holds the binding-code sticky pinned since 1981. The sticky reads as if it's about horseshoes and copper wire, but per the W11 glossary it's the original demon-binding code in the foal register. Two other threads with WIRE_MOTHER's practical voice.

threads.subject: STICKY · the work that has to be done before you bring the foal in

op.body:
Sticky. Read this before you post in the barn.

  1. The foal is brought into the barn at dusk. Not before.
  2. The barn door is the only door. The barn has no other doors.
  3. The copper at the lintel is not decoration. The copper at the lintel is the lintel.
  4. The salt at the threshold is the salt the foal walks over. The foal will refuse the salt the first time. The foal does not refuse the salt the second time. If the foal refuses the salt the second time, the foal is not your foal.
  5. The name you give the foal is the name the foal answers to. The name the foal answers to is the name no one else uses. If someone else uses the name, the foal is not your foal anymore.
  6. The horseshoe over the door is hung points up so the luck stays in. The luck staying in is the foal staying in.
  7. When the foal is in, the door closes. The door does not close again until dawn.

This is the work. Do the work. — WM.

threads.subject: the panel at the cooper place · rewire or replace

op.body:
The panel at the cooper place is a 1962 FPE. The breakers don't trip. The breakers haven't tripped since '88. The breakers are not going to trip.

Replace, don't rewire. The new panel goes in Monday. If you have a foal in the barn at the cooper place, take it out Sunday night. — WM.

replies.body: Confirmed FPE — we replaced four of them at the parish in '94 for the same reason. The breakers in those didn't trip either.

threads.subject: the fourteenth year on the rope · the foal is fourteen

op.body:
Foals.

Fifteen years ago the sticky was written for a foal that was four months old. The foal grew. The foal is fourteen years on the rope this fall. The work that was written for the four-month-old does not cover the fourteen-year-old. The work was correct for the four-month-old. The work is correct for the four-month-old still. The work is not the whole work for the fourteen-year-old.

The family is going to do the rest of the work this week. Whatever the family picks, the foal is a person now and the person is going to decide some of it.

If you are reading this and you have a foal that is fourteen, you know the year. If you don't, you don't. — WM.

replies.body:
The pattern of the fourteenth year is the pattern of the fortieth year inverted. The foal has more agency than the matriarch had at the same age, because the matriarch did the work that gave the foal the agency. The matriarch has less agency than the foal in this room because the room is the foal's room.

The matriarch knows this. The matriarch wrote the sticky knowing this. — h.

threads.subject: the demon question · per the W11 thread on RUST_CODE

op.body:
Foals — the W11 thread on RUST_CODE has asked the question the sticky was written for. I am not going to answer the question here because the answer is the sticky and the sticky is fifteen years old and the sticky is correct.

If you are reading this and the sticky has read to you like a barn-and-foal post, read it again. The barn is the body. The foal is the thing the body holds. The copper, the salt, the name, the horseshoe — those are the work.

The rest of the question is the matriarch's question and I will answer it in DM if you DM me. — WM.

threads.subject: SUBSTATION · the computer game somebody left in the mailbox · findings

op.body:
Somebody left a computer game in the barn's mailbox with a note asking if it's right. The game is SUBSTATION. Bois d'Arc, out of Houston, 1993. You are the night maintenance shift at a substation. The substation reads numbers on Tuesdays at 3:14 AM and the game wants you to decode them.

I ran it on the shop 386 over two evenings. Findings:

  1. The lockout-tagout sequence in the game is correct. Correct order, correct tags, correct wait. That is not in any public manual. Somebody on that game has held a red tag in their hand.
  2. The bus arrangement on screen is a real arrangement. I know the arrangement.
  3. The numbers. The game treats the numbers as a puzzle. Rule for the barn: the numbers are not a puzzle. If a substation near you reads you numbers at 3:14 on a Tuesday, you do not decode. You put your tools in the truck, you leave the yard, and you post here.

The game is honest work. The subject of the game is not a game. Both things are true. Keep the foal clear of the fence at the yard on Route 9 regardless.

— W.M.

replies.body: WIRE_MOTHER I own SUBSTATION, bought the SNES one for the soundtrack. I have decoded the Tuesday numbers maybe forty times. In the game. Am I allowed to keep playing it? Genuine question. — j.

Play the game. The game is the fence, not the yard. The rule is for the yard.

— W.M.
